whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before You Wait

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it helps to act early.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your compensation is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your claim isn't artificially capped just because your injuries are hard to put a price on.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover Money
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you don't pay out of pocket to have your case reviewed or pursued. Legal fees only come out of a settlement or award if you win.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Firebaugh?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If your injury involved a government vehicle or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Firebaugh?
items.answer: Public collision records show N Street, Rt 33, Clyde Fannon Road, and N Dos Palos Road as the corridors with the highest reported collision counts in the city. These are simply the roads where incidents are most frequently logged, not a judgment about any particular stretch.
